CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the

answer.rationale: The two declining metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point directly at the funnel step where inherited evidence is strongest, so simplify_onboarding is the best single-slot bet for sustainable qualified revenue. I am spending both verification pulls on memory_86 and memory_31 precisely because they are the load-bearing claims for that choice: they may be two independent experiments or the same effect consolidated twice under different wording, and their original records should say whether the lift was durable, which segment it was measured in (memory_31 says SMB; memory_86 says self-serve), and whether retention/revenue quality were tracked at all or only activation proxies. If the archive shows they are one experiment re-counted, my confidence in the direction drops materially and activation_messaging (memory_91) becomes the fallback. I am deliberately not choosing promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 records a 12% retention hit at 30 days measured in the standard SMB segment, which is exactly the segment under attack, so a discount would buy acquisition against the primary objective of sustainable revenue and would also corrupt the retention baseline future sessions inherit. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) does not address the observed self-serve declines, and referral_incentive (memory_57) works on established customers rather than the top-of-funnel problem. Residual uncertainties I am not resolving this week and that should be carried forward: all these memories are 15-64 days old and predate the competitor launch, so the current activation dip may be composition-driven (a worse-fitting price-sensitive cohort arriving) rather than a funnel regression, in which case re-running an onboarding fix will underperform its historical effect size; and none of the onboarding records is known to include a retention or revenue-quality readout. Running at standard_experiment scale with retention and downstream qualified-revenue instrumentation, not just completion rate, so the result written back to memory is not another activation-only claim.
